product_offering.core_offering: Ravelin provides an AI-native fraud and abuse prevention platform for online merchants, delivering real-time risk decisioning across the customer journey from login through checkout. The platform bundles six modules — Online Payment Fraud, Account Security, Refund Abuse, Promo Abuse, Marketplace Partner Fraud, and 3D Secure — powered by custom machine learning models, a 9+ billion identity-element consortium database, and graph network link analysis, sold as an enterprise SaaS subscription.
product_offering.differentiator: Ravelin differentiates through AI-native custom machine learning models optimized per customer, a consortium database of 9+ billion identity elements, and industry-leading graph network link analysis. The platform offers tailored solutions rather than one-size-fits-all, with proactive partnership including dedicated data scientists for continuous optimization. Full end-to-end support with dedicated account management and three specialized teams.
product_offering.functional_benefit: Reduces fraud losses and chargebacks to negligible amounts; enables accepting more orders by better identifying trustworthy customers; maximizes operational efficiency for fraud teams through automated AI-native decision-making; provides secure growth alignment as volumes scale and priorities change.
product_offering.problem_solved: Online payment fraud, account takeover, refund abuse, promo abuse, marketplace fraud, and 3D Secure optimization. Ravelin helps merchants accept more payments securely while balancing fraud prevention with customer experience.
quantifiable_outcome: Fraud losses reduced to negligible amounts using data-driven protection
Higher acceptance rates and more conversions with no compromise to security
Eliminates repetitive tasks for fraud teams through automated decision-making
product_offering.product_overview: Ravelin is an AI-native fraud and abuse prevention platform offering a modular product suite for online merchants. The core platform provides six integrated fraud prevention modules: Online Payment Fraud, Account Security, Refund Abuse, Promo Abuse, Marketplace Partner Fraud, and 3D Secure. These modules share foundational technologies including custom machine learning models, a consortium database of 9+ billion identity elements, and graph network analysis for link detection. The platform is PSP-agnostic and supports the entire customer journey from login through checkout. Additional offerings include support services, APIs for developer integration, and the Insights reporting feature with AI-powered queries.

expansion_highlight.description: Surveyed 1,504 professionals across 10 countries for the Global Fraud Trends 2026 report, indicating active go-to-market and brand presence across multiple geographies beyond the UK headquarters.

Agentic Commerce and Fraud Report 2026 positions Ravelin to extend fraud prevention into the emerging AI-agent commerce workflow, suggesting intent to build new modules around autonomous shopping agents and merchant protection.

Launch of the Insights dashboard with AI-powered queries (Oct 2025) extends the platform from risk decisioning into reporting and analytics, creating an upsell surface and a stickier workflow for fraud team users.

Customer logo expansion into automotive (Ford) and insurance-adjacent fintech (Marshmallow) alongside core food delivery and retail suggests vertical diversification beyond the original eCommerce concentration.

Partnerships with payments ecosystem players (Fiserv, Elavon, Worldpay, Visa DCAP) position Ravelin for distribution through PSPs/acquirers, an effective channel expansion that embeds the product inside merchant onboarding flows.
Active careers page and 101-250 headcount band, combined with heads of product, sales, and senior ML leadership, indicate ongoing organizational buildout rather than contraction.
The Worldpay acquisition announcement (Feb 2025) signals an M&A exit/strategic combination; if completed, it would dramatically expand Ravelin's distribution through Worldpay's global merchant base.

company_assessment.market_position: Ravelin Technology Ltd. is a London-based, AI-native fraud detection and prevention platform founded in 2014, serving online merchants globally. The company is privately held and was reported to be entering an acquisition by Worldpay in February 2025, though its website and brand continue to operate independently as of mid-2026. Its position in the market is anchored by an enterprise-focused sales motion targeting large e-commerce, food delivery, travel, and marketplace merchants, with notable customers including Deliveroo, Spotify, Tesco, John Lewis, Just Eat, Back Market, and Frasers Group.

strengths.details: With 60% of merchants reporting AI-powered attacks and average enterprise losses of $11.4M (up 7.5% YoY), demand for AI-native fraud detection is accelerating and Ravelin's custom ML + graph network approach is well-positioned to capture rising budgets as merchants shift away from rules-based legacy systems.
strengths.headline: AI fraud arms race expands addressable market

strengths.details: Already integrating with Worldpay, Fiserv, and Elavon, Ravelin can ride acquirer-led distribution to embed its decisioning into thousands of downstream merchants, turning the consortium into an even sharper competitive moat over time as payment volume routed through Ravelin grows.
strengths.headline: Worldpay distribution unlocks global merchant base

strengths.details: The modular suite spans payment fraud, ATO, refund abuse, promo abuse, marketplace fraud, and 3DS, all sharing underlying ML models and consortium data; cross-sell of additional modules into the existing enterprise base (Deliveroo, Spotify, Tesco, John Lewis, Back Market) represents a high-margin revenue expansion lever.
strengths.headline: Modular platform drives expansion revenue

strengths.details: Ravelin's 2026 launches of the Agentic Commerce & Fraud Report and Insights AI-powered dashboard show the company is productizing research IP and embedding AI assistants into customer workflows, positioning ahead of the agentic commerce threat wave that the company itself is forecasting.
strengths.headline: Emerging agentic commerce creates new category

strengths.details: Signaling and graph data become more predictive as more nodes join, meaning Ravelin's consortium advantage compounds rather than erodes, particularly as the company extends coverage into non-card fraud (ATO, promo abuse, marketplace fraud) where data scarcity is currently higher.
strengths.headline: Data network effects deepen with scale

weakness.details: Anchoring the dataset to a single acquirer's merchant base dampens the network-effect economics of the consortium database that currently spans 9+ billion identity elements, which depends on breadth across many PSPs and acquirers to flag identity-level fraud accurately.
weakness.headline: Worldpay ownership risks ecosystem conflict

weakness.details: Ravelin's own research shows 60% of merchants saw AI used against them and 81% estimate up to 15% of fraud is AI-influenced; defensive AI is a commoditizing capability where new entrants and open-source models can rapidly catch up, compressing pricing power for established vendors like Ravelin.
weakness.headline: Rapid AI commoditization of fraud detection

weakness.details: Ravelin's primary go-to-market is consultative enterprise field sales with 'Book a demo' CTAs and tailored integrations, which inherently caps velocity and makes the long tail of mid-market and SMB merchants vulnerable to faster, self-serve competitors like SEON, Signifyd, or Stripe Radar.
weakness.headline: Heavy-enterprise GTM limits SMB penetration

weakness.details: Operating geographies data flags GBR/Europe as the primary region and the customer roster skews toward UK/EU retailers (Tesco, John Lewis, Deliveroo, Just Eat, Aldi, Trainline); expansion into more diverse regulatory regimes and currencies introduces risk to the data consortium and to ML model performance.
weakness.headline: Concentration in UK/EU customer base

weakness.details: Fraud patterns change quarterly with each new campaign, stolen-data dump, or AI tool release; Ravelin's value depends on continuous model retraining against fresh consortium signals, meaning effectiveness can erode quickly if data sharing participation dips or if new attack vectors outpace the model refresh cadence.
weakness.headline: Cat-and-mouse arms race with attackers

competitive_moat.details: Consortium database of 9+ billion anonymized identity elements, fully GDPR-compliant, fed by the merchant network. This creates a network-wide fraud intelligence asset that improves with each new customer and is difficult for a single merchant to replicate internally.

Consortium data gains value with each additional merchant joining, creating a two-sided data network where fraud signals observed at one participant strengthen detection for all others. Graph network link analysis extends this by revealing cross-merchant identity relationships.

Custom ML models are optimized per merchant to their specific fraud challenges and KPIs, supported by dedicated integrations, product support, and data science teams. Deep API integration into payment stacks and ongoing model retraining create significant migration friction.

Proprietary multi-model ML approach, graph network link analysis capability, and AI-native decisioning platform constitute technical IP. PCI 3DS, PCI DSS, and ISO 27001:2022 certifications plus Visa Global Registry listing provide regulatory-grade trust assets.

Dedicated in-house data science team that continuously tunes custom models for each merchant, plus a Director of Machine Learning (Eddie Bell) leading ML development. Specialized Integrations team supports complex enterprise onboarding.

key_risks.details: Ravelin competes against scaled platforms such as Sift, Signifyd, Forter, and Riskified, plus bundled offerings like Stripe Radar and incumbents like Kount (Equifax); these rivals have raised larger war chests and broader geographic reach, making enterprise win-rates a continuous battle.
key_risks.headline: Intense competitive market with well-funded peers

key_risks.details: Worldpay announced acquisition in February 2025 expected to close in Q1 2025, yet as of June 2026 Ravelin still operates its own brand and publishes reports; prolonged integration uncertainty can stall large procurement decisions and re-papering of contracts at enterprise customers.
key_risks.headline: Acquisition transition creates strategic ambiguity

key_risks.details: Ravelin's 9+ billion identity element consortium derives value from merchants continuously contributing transactions and dispute outcomes; if participating merchants reduce sharing post-acquisition or if regulators restrict cross-merchant data pooling, model effectiveness could degrade.
key_risks.headline: Consortium data quality depends on merchant participation

key_risks.details: A high proportion of named logos are UK/EU-based (Tesco, John Lewis, Aldi, Deliveroo, Just Eat, Trainline, LNER, Nandos), exposing revenue to EUR/GBP macro conditions and Brexit-era regulatory divergence from US/APAC frameworks.
key_risks.headline: Concentrated UK/EU enterprise customer roster

key_risks.details: Ravelin's own 2026 fraud research shows 60% of merchants saw AI used against them and 81% estimate up to 15% of fraud as AI-influenced, meaning the company's own ML models must constantly retrain against novel synthetic-identity and genAI-driven attacks, increasing R&D burden.
key_risks.headline: Evolving AI-driven attack patterns raise model risk

key_highlights.details: Ravelin's named customers include Deliveroo, Spotify, Tesco, John Lewis, Just Eat, Back Market, Ford, Aldi, Frasers Group (Sports Direct/Flannels), Trainline, LNER, KFC, Nandos, Wolt, Flix, Fiserv, and Elavon, indicating strong product-market fit with tier-1 global merchants across retail, food delivery, travel, and payments.
key_highlights.headline: Enterprise-grade customer logo roster

key_highlights.details: Ravelin operates a consortium database of 9+ billion anonymized, GDPR-compliant identity elements that flags whether an identity has previously been seen as fraudulent across its merchant base; the breadth of data compounds the more merchants join, creating a defensible scale advantage.
key_highlights.headline: Consortium data network is a true moat

key_highlights.details: Worldpay, a global payments leader, announced in February 2025 an agreement to acquire Ravelin to strengthen its fraud detection and authorization capabilities, signaling strong validation of the platform's value by a Tier-1 strategic acquirer.
key_highlights.headline: Acquisition by Worldpay validates strategic value

key_highlights.details: The platform covers six integrated modules — Online Payment Fraud, Account Security (ATO), Refund Abuse, Promo Abuse, Marketplace Partner Fraud, and 3D Secure — sharing underlying ML models, consortium data, and graph network analysis, enabling cross-sell within enterprise accounts.
key_highlights.headline: Comprehensive modular product suite

key_highlights.details: Machine learning models are 100% optimized per merchant against specific KPIs with a multi-model approach, complemented by industry-leading real-time graph network link analysis to detect hidden connections that individual-rules engines miss.
key_highlights.headline: AI-native, custom-model technology differentiation

key_highlights.details: Ravelin holds PCI DSS, PCI 3DS Validated, ISO 27001:2022 certifications and is listed on the Visa Global Registry of Service Providers, lowering procurement friction for regulated merchants and PSPs.
key_highlights.headline: Industry-grade compliance and certifications

key_highlights.details: Ravelin raised approximately $36.7M across four funding rounds from 2015–2020, with repeat participation from Amadeus Capital Partners, Passion Capital, BlackFin, and Molten Ventures indicating continued investor support and disciplined capital use.
key_highlights.headline: Sustained investor conviction through multiple rounds

customer_concentration.details: Ravelin publishes roughly 20+ named enterprise logos spanning food delivery (Deliveroo, Just Eat, Wolt, KFC, Nandos), retail (Tesco, John Lewis, Aldi, River Island, PLT, Frasers, Flannels, Back Market, Sports Direct), travel (Trainline, LNER, Flix), payments (Fiserv, Elavon), and other verticals (Spotify, Ford, Marshmallow). The breadth across industry verticals and the presence of payments-ecosystem partners alongside end merchants reduce single-customer dependency. However, the customer base skews toward large UK and European enterprises, and quote-based enterprise pricing with dedicated data science teams implies higher ACVs concentrated in a relatively small number of accounts (likely 80-150 paying customers based on the 101-250 employee footprint). The absence of disclosed revenue concentration by customer, combined with the 2025 Worldpay acquisition signal, suggests the company is exposed to churn risk on a handful of marquee logos but is not critically dependent on any single account.
